title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. U_{0,3} = P^1 \ {0,1,∞} carries the S_3 action permuting the three punctures. The orbifold (U_{0,3}, S_3) has U_{0,3}/S_3 ≅ the j-line, so it is essentially the coarse M_{1,1}. U_{0,3} is also the level-2 modular curve M_{1,1}[2]', with coordinate the Legendre λ.

Previous page. The upper half plane D maps to U_{0,3}^{an} through λ, i.e. U_{0,3}^{an} ≅ D/Γ(2). This map is equivariant for SL(2,Z)' → SL(2,Z/2) ≅ S_3, where SL(2,Z)' is most plausibly PSL(2,Z) = SL(2,Z)/±1. So D is a universal cover of the orbifold (U_{0,3}, S_3), and SL(2,Z)' is its 'mixed' fundamental group relative to that cover.

This page.
- To identify SL(2,Z)' with π_1((U_{0,3}, S_3); P) for the base point P = -J̄ = e^{iπ/3}, one must choose a point of D over P. The base point is a point with nontrivial S_3-stabilizer: of λ, the order-3 subgroup fixes exactly e^{±iπ/3}.
- The choice is ambiguous up to the kernel of PSL(2,Z) → S_3, i.e. Γ(2)/±1. This kernel is free of rank 2 and isomorphic to π_{0,3} = π_1(U_{0,3}), as he says.
- He proposes the canonical choice τ = J = ρ = e^{2πi/3}, the elliptic point of order 3. One must check that λ(ρ) = P and not P̄ = -J; otherwise one would take τ = -J̄ = ρ+1 = e^{iπ/6·2} instead.
- NB. The three elements of PSL(2,Z) sending ρ to ρ+1 are T = (1 1; 0 1), (1 0; 1 1) and S = (0 -1; 1 0). Check: ρ+1 = -ρ̄; ρ/(ρ+1) = -ρ^{-1} = -ρ̄; -1/ρ = -ρ̄. There are exactly three because Stab(ρ+1) has order 3.
- None of them is ≡ I mod 2. Hence ρ and ρ+1 are not Γ(2)-equivalent, so their images in D/Γ(2) are the two distinct points -J and -J̄ (in some order).
- Next page. The choice is characterized by τ being a root of unity. This 'normalizes' the homomorphism (73) (the identification of π_1's) into an effective one.

Purpose. Fix a canonical isomorphism between the orbifold fundamental group of M_{1,1} (presented as (U_{0,3}, S_3)), based at an elliptic point, and PSL(2,Z). This prepares the 'équation des lacets' / Teichmüller-tower computations. Grothendieck then remarks that a profinite version would need foundations he lacks.
errors: No substantive error. The NB computation is correct: exactly three elements of PSL(2,Z) send ρ to ρ+1, and none is ≡ I mod 2.
Which of ρ, ρ+1 lies over e^{iπ/3} depends on the normalization of λ; Grothendieck leaves the verification implicit ('or inversely' on the next page).

ideas.what: D → U_{0,3}^{an} = D/Γ(2) (Legendre λ) as universal cover of the orbifold (U_{0,3}, S_3), with PSL(2,Z) → S_3 as the action on groups of operators
ideas.modern_name: orbifold uniformization of the level-2 modular curve / M_{1,1} as orbifold quotient [P^1\{0,1,∞}/S_3]
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Klein, Fricke; modern orbifold language Thurston); in GT context Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Related remarks on M_{1,1} and SL(2,Z) in Esquisse d'un programme; details unsure

ideas.what: Fundamental group based at an orbifold (elliptic) point, defined via a choice of point in the universal cover; ambiguity = kernel Γ(2)/±1 ≅ π_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: orbifold/stack fundamental group with base point at a stacky point; 'mixed π_1'
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (orbifold π_1: Thurston; stacky π_1: Noohi, Zoonekynd)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (circulated 1981) discusses π_1 of multiplicities; unsure exact place

ideas.what: Canonical normalization by choosing τ = ρ = e^{2πi/3} over the base point, verified by showing ρ and ρ+1 are not Γ(2)-equivalent
ideas.modern_name: choice of elliptic point ρ as base point for PSL(2,Z) ≅ Z/2 * Z/3

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but classical bookkeeping: a base point at an elliptic point and the Γ(2) non-congruence of ρ and ρ+1. The only hint of something more is the next-page remark about lacking a profinite theory of 'tronçons', which is not on this page.
transcription_corrections: 'Sl(2,Z)' ≃ GPl(1,Z)^+ [?]': the image is hard to read; possibly 'PGl(2,Z)^+' or similar notation for SL(2,Z)/±1, uncertain.
'en vérifiant [?] des bois [?] pour': the image looks closer to 'en tranchant des bois pour' (meaning unclear); reading uncertain.
'comme c'est −J̄ = …': the word before 'c'est' looks like 'sinon' (i.e. 'sinon c'est −J̄ … qu'on choisirait'), which fits the logic better.
Last line: 'J et −J̄ [ont des images dans] ne sont pas congrus' — the struck phrase may be 'ont des images dans un…', with 'ne sont pas congrus' written after the strike.
